In a patient at risk (cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B, prior hepatocellular carcinoma), hepatocellular carcinoma is diagnosed by imaging without biopsy if the lesion meets the LI-RADS major criteria: non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement (APHE), nonperipheral washout (the lesion becomes darker than the liver in the portal or delayed phase), enhancing capsule and growth above threshold. A lesion ≥ 20 mm with APHE and at least one other criterion is LR-5.
Here all the typical features are present: hypodensity on unenhanced images, heterogeneous "mosaic" arterial enhancement (enhancing areas separated by septa, with a nodule-in-nodule appearance), washout and capsule in the portal phase.
Pitfalls: 1) the arterial phase must be late (portal branches already opacified); in the early arterial phase APHE can be missed. 2) Washout is judged relative to the liver, not relative to the arterial phase: in the portal phase the lesion has the same absolute density, but the surrounding liver enhances much more. 3) Size is measured from outer edge to outer edge, including the capsule. 4) Rim hyperenhancement, peripheral washout or targetoid restriction point to LR-M (cholangiocarcinoma, metastasis). 5) Before categorizing, always check the portal vein and hepatic veins: enhancing tissue in the lumen = LR-TIV, which changes stage and treatment.
The site is described by Couinaud segments: the hepatic veins separate the sectors (the middle one between right and left, the right one between anterior sector 5-8 and posterior sector 6-7), the plane of the portal bifurcation separates the upper segments (7, 8, 4a) from the lower ones (6, 5, 4b). This lesion is above the portal bifurcation, lateral to the middle hepatic vein, in the right anterior sector: segment 8.
